chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Abbas ibn 'Amir from Aban ibn 'Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who marries a slave woman while having a free woman, he said: 'He does not marry the slave woman in addition to the free woman, but he maries the free woman in addition to the slave woman, and the free woman gets two nights and the slave woman gets one night.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dividing time between a free wife and a slave concubine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the classical Shia jurisprudence regarding polygyny with concubines, establishing that a man may hold one free wife alongside multiple slave women, but not multiple free wives simultaneously. It prescribes a specific distribution of nights, granting the free wife two nights for every one night allocated to each slave concubine, reflecting the hierarchical status and rights within the household structure of the early Islamic period.
